advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.allowConcurrentLabel: Allow ComfyUI and LM Studio to run at the same time
advanced.allowConcurrentHint: By default, image generation and LM Studio (chat/vision/prompt-assist) take turns so they don't fight over the same GPU on a shared server. Turn this on only if your hardware has enough headroom to run both at once.
advanced.commonQueueLabel: Common queue for ComfyUI and LM Studio
advanced.commonQueueHint: Stricter than the option above: only one job runs at a time across BOTH ComfyUI and LM Studio, in a single shared queue — even two ComfyUI generations from different clients won't overlap. Overrides "Allow ComfyUI and LM Studio to run at the same time" when both are on.

agents.navDesc: Connect Claude Desktop, ChatGPT and Bionic
agents.title: Agents
agents.desc: Let your AI assistant create and edit images here, through MCP. Everything below is already filled in with this installation's folder and port.
agents.needApp: Nomad Studio must stay open (and ComfyUI running) while the assistant works.
claudeSteps: Add the "nomad-studio" block inside "mcpServers" (paste all of it if the file is empty).
Quit Claude completely (also from the icon next to the clock) and open it again.
agents.codexNote: Only in the desktop app's Codex and ChatGPT Work modes: regular ChatGPT chat accepts remote servers only.
codexSteps: Press Ctrl + , → Integrations → Plugins → Add → Add MCP Server. Type STDIO, name nomad_studio, and fill in the command, arguments and variables below.
Or, with the app closed, add this block to the config file (it also gives long generations 10 minutes).
Open the app again. It asks before generating or editing; lookups don't need it.
antigravitySteps: In the Agent panel, open the … menu → MCP Servers → Manage MCP Servers → View raw config.
Add the "nomad-studio" block inside "mcpServers" (paste all of it if the file is empty).
Go back to Manage MCP Servers and press Refresh, or close Antigravity and open it again.
bionicSteps: Open Bionic's MCP servers settings and add one: name Nomad Studio, type stdio, and the command, arguments and variables below.
Or, with Bionic closed, add this entry to the "servers" list of the config file.
Restart Bionic and load a model with tool use (best in our tests: Ornith 1.5 9B).

agents.restartAntigravity: In Antigravity, press Refresh in Manage MCP Servers, or open it again.

format.changeLater: You can change this in Settings at any time. Images already saved are not converted.
format.loss1: Very smooth gradients (skies, plain backgrounds) can show slight bands.
format.loss2: Sharp edges and fine detail (text, thin lines, pixel art) can look a little softer.
format.loss3: Film grain and noise can get smoothed out.
format.loss4: Loss cannot be undone, and it adds up if the same image is retouched and saved many times. You can choose the format for a single generation in Advanced.
format.pngText: Keeps every pixel exactly, with no loss.
format.soonNote: Your choice is saved now. Images keep being saved as PNG until WebP support is finished.

models.title: Language models
models.lead: Some flows use a model in LM Studio to write prompts and describe images. None is required, but we recommend having at least one. These are the four we measured.
models.needLms: LM Studio has to be running to check and install models. Go back to the LM Studio step, or skip this for now.
models.detecting: Looking for models in LM Studio…
models.none: None of the recommended models is installed. We recommend installing at least one.
models.dlFailed: LM Studio could not download it.
models.meta: {size} GB on disk · comfortable on {vram} GB of video memory
models.bgHint: Downloads run inside LM Studio and keep going even if you close this page.

desc.qwythos-9b: Good at everything, writing and vision. Our default on 8 GB cards.
desc.ornith-1.5-9b: The same, with the smallest memory footprint we measured.
desc.gemma-4-12b: Strict JSON and templates, and the best at describing images at the length you ask for.
desc.ministral-3-14b: Always thinks before answering: the most detailed image reads, slower on batches of prompts.

network.remoteLms: Is LM Studio on another computer?
network.sameNetwork: Both computers must be on the same network.
network.comfyListen: On that computer, start ComfyUI with --listen 0.0.0.0 (in ComfyUI Desktop, set the server listen address to 0.0.0.0).
network.lmsServe: On that computer, open LM Studio › Developer and turn on "Serve on Local Network".
network.privateFirewall: In Windows on that computer, set the network as Private and allow the program in the firewall when asked.
network.typeAddress: Type its address here, e.g. http://192.168.1.20:{port}, or search your network again.
network.searchingFor: Looking for {name} on this computer and on your network…
network.otherComputerNote: It runs on another computer on your network.

apps.vcText: This computer does not have it yet, and without it ComfyUI closes as soon as it starts.
apps.vcNote: About 25 MB from Microsoft. Windows will ask for your permission once.
apps.vcInstalling: Installing the Visual C++ Runtime… Windows asks for permission: answer Yes. If you do not see its window, click the blinking icon in the taskbar.

apps.preferPortable: The portable build is the one Nomad Studio works best with.
apps.listen: Let other computers on my network use it
apps.installerOpen: Finish the installation in the window that just opened. If you do not see it, click its icon in the taskbar.
apps.lmsNote: Its installer opens by itself; we wait for you here.
apps.lmsNoteLinux: LM Studio from its official website, about 1 GB. It opens by itself when it is ready, and it is added to your applications. No administrator password.
apps.lmsManual: Install it from its website, open it once and come back here: Nomad Studio finds it by itself.
apps.phasePython: Getting a Python of its own for ComfyUI…
apps.phaseTorch: Installing PyTorch for {backend}… this is the long part.
apps.phaseReqs: Installing the rest of what ComfyUI needs…
apps.cpuOnlyLinux: PyTorch has no build for this graphics card on Linux, so ComfyUI will run on the processor: it works, but each image takes minutes.
apps.installNoteLinux: ComfyUI from its official release, with a Python of its own and PyTorch for {backend}: 1 to 5 GB depending on the card. No administrator password needed.
apps.cpuOnlyNoGpu: No graphics card PyTorch can use was found here, so ComfyUI will run on the processor: it works, but each image takes minutes.
